newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SLEIGHTHOLME PICKED TO SERVE COUNTRY, NOT CLUB.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SLEIGHTHOLME PICKED TO SERVE COUNTRY, NOT CLUB.

text.p: England winger Jon Sleightholme experienced the rare sensation of being dropped by his club and re-selected by his country on the same morning on Wednesday.
Sleightholme, who scored a try against the New Zealand Barbarians at Twickenham and did a fair job marking Jonah Lomu, is in a 23-man England squad for the test against Argentina on December 14.
But his place on the wing for Bath in their crunch league fixture against Harlequins this Saturday has been taken by rugby league star Jason Robinson.

Sleightholme, who has scored on his last three international appearances, is merely a replacement in a Bath team which sees Argentine international Federico Mendez and US Eagles captain Dan Lyle make their league debuts.
Mendez, who has signed an 18-month contract worth 135,000 pounds ($222,000), made a huge impression during the 36-17 victory over Western Samoa this week.

Further worrying news for Sleightholme is the return of Tony Underwood to the England squad after 18 months absence. Prop Victor Ubogu has also been added to the squad, which will be trimmed next week.
Underwood has not played for England since earning a nightmare 20th cap against Lomu and the All Blacks in the World Cup semifinal in Cape Town, but is now back in the frame.

"When Tony returned to his best, he had to come into consideration. He can play left or right and it will be two wings from the three we have named when we make our selection on Monday," said coach Jack Rowell.
